live_high.selection: St Finbarrs To Win (1.62 / -161; St Finbarrs -1.5 pts handicap)
live_high.text: St Finbarrs to win at 1.62 (-161) is the match-winner selection against Nemo Rangers in Cork's Premier Senior Football Championship Final. Cork GAA lists the decider at SuperValu Pairc Ui Chaoimh on Sunday 25 October, starting at 4.00pm. Nemo's knockout route included a 1-20 to 1-17 win over Castlehaven and a 1-15 to 0-16 semi-final victory against Carrigaline. The Barrs defeated Clonakilty 2-12 to 0-16 in their semi-final after beating Carbery, for which this event page supplies no score. The selection rests on St Finbarrs' scoring in that latest tie, not an assumed Carbery winning margin. Nemo's narrow semi-final success keeps this a competitive final rather than a one-sided forecast.

live_high.text: Back MT Melsungen to win at 1.54 (-185) in Wednesday's Group B trip to SC Jane Sandanski in Skopje (18:45 CET). Melsungen sit second in Group B on 6 points (3-0-2, 138:138) with a Main Round berth on the line after defeating group leaders Wisla Plock 28:26 in Round 5 behind goalkeeper Nebojsa Simic's 11 saves (including three straight crunch-time stops) and six goals apiece from Eric Balenciaga (6/6) and Aaron Mensing. Fourth-placed HC Vardar 1961 (1-0-4, 2 points, 154:158) are already eliminated from Main Round contention despite upsetting Nantes 33:27 behind Leon Ljevar's 7/9 shooting, and Melsungen already beat Vardar at home in Round 1. Melsungen to win is our call.

live_high.text: Cucine Lube Civitanova to win the match at 1.44 (-227) is the call against Pallavolo Padova at Eurosuole Forum. Lube's opening sweep of Verona produced 78 rally points and only 65 conceded, placing them fourth in the league table with three points. Padova enter eleventh after a straight-sets defeat to Piacenza, scoring 56 points against 75. The contrast is in both attack and resistance, not simply the result column: Civitanova cleared their first test without dropping a set, whereas Padova have yet to claim one. Those opening-round figures favor Lube, though one match is too small a sample to treat this as a certainty.

live_high.text: Take Vero Volley Monza to win the match at 1.61 (-164) against Rana Verona. The league calendar puts this second-round meeting at OpiquadArena on 25 October. Monza stand eighth and Verona ninth, both without a point after one fixture, so neither side has a successful opening result to fall back on. Monza nevertheless kept the rally-point balance close in losing 1-3 to Prata, 91 scored to 94 conceded; Verona's 0-3 loss to Civitanova was wider at 65-78. That relative competitiveness supports the home selection. It does not establish a reception-efficiency edge or any individual player's availability, neither of which is assumed here.

live_high.selection: Sir Susa Scai Perugia Match Winner (1.58 / -172)
live_high.text: Sir Susa Scai Perugia to win at 1.58 (-172) is the match-winner selection at Pala Barton Energy in Perugia, scheduled for 17:00 UTC on 25 October. Prata di Pordenone arrive with three league points from a 3-1 win over Monza, while Perugia collected two after needing five sets to beat Cuneo. The points table therefore warns against dismissing the visitors. Perugia's 114-95 rally-point line from that opener was stronger than Prata's 94-91, which is the statistical reason to prefer them in their own arena despite sitting one place lower. The selection is Perugia outright; no set handicap or total is being recommended from these figures.
